name: Inference without Interference: Disaggregate LLM Inference for Mixed Downstream Workloads (TetriInfer)
affiliations: Southern University of Science and Technology
problem: A production cluster mixes downstream tasks with very different prompt and output length distributions, and co-locating them means prefill-heavy and decode-heavy requests interfere destructively.
mechanism: Three pillars. (1) Partition prompts into fixed-size chunks so the accelerator stays near its compute-saturated limit. (2) Disaggregate prefill and decode instances so each runs independently. (3) A two-level scheduling algorithm augmented with PREDICTED resource usage, to avoid decode scheduling hotspots.
speedup_reported: Per the arXiv abstract: uses 38% less resources while lowering average TTFT by 97% and average job completion time (JCT) by 47%. Baselines are not named in the abstract; the metric is performance per dollar for mixed downstream workloads, which is why the resource reduction and the latency reduction can both be large at once.
